32-10903.title: Registered Interior Designer
32-10903.description: Interior designers may apply for registration in Nevada, however, in order to do interior design of commercial spaces, designers must be registered. To qualify for a certificate to practice as a Registered Interior Designer, an applicant must: 1) Have successfully completed a program of interior design accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA) or a substantially equivalent program approved by the Board. 2) Have at least 2 years of experience* in interior design, and 3a) Pass the National Council for Interior Design Qualification (NCIDQ) exam (October 2000 or later); or 3b) Pass any prior version of the NCIDQ and the Nevada Supplemental Examination for Registered Interior Designers. *Note: Applicants may gain the required experience through the Interior Design Experience Program (IDEP). IDEP is a monitored, documented experience program administered by the NCIDQ for graduates of interior design education programs. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application-$25; NCIDQ exam application review - $210; NCIDQ exam (3 parts) - $210; Nevada Supplemental Exam - $100; certificate of registration - $125; annual renewal - $150; non-CIDA education evaluation (to determine substantial equivalency)--$300; stamp--$25.
32-10903.agency: Board of Architecture, Interior Design, & Residential Design

32-22101.title: Interpreter for the Deaf and Hearing Impaired
32-22101.description: Interpreters for the deaf and hearing impaired, and providers of real-time captioning must be registered to practice in Nevada. Applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old and have a high school diploma or G.E.D. 2) Meet the education, training, experience and certification requirements established by the Aging and Disability Services Division for the applicable professional classification (community, education or communication access realtime translation (CART)) and level (apprentice, skilled, intermediate, advanced or master.) Contact the Aging and Disability Services unit for more information. The Nevada Revised Statute (656A.100) establishing the requirements to interpret in Nevada is available online. Web Site Location: http://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-656A.html
32-22101.agency: Department of Health and Human Services · Aging and Disability Services Division

32-20501.title: Nevada Certified Court Interpreter
32-20501.description: Applicants for Certified Court Interpreter must: 1) Complete the orientation workshop for interpreters in Nevada courts offered by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC). 2) Pass the Nevada written exam given by the AOC (minimum score of 80%). 3) Pass the Nevada oral exam given by the AOC (minimum score of 70%), 4) Obtain 40 hours of Nevada court observation or work within the 12 months immediately preceding request for certification, 5) Submit the Certification Request form which includes a criminal history check, 6) Swear to the required oath and the Code of Professional Responsibility for Interpreters in Nevada courts. Applicants for Registered Interpreter (applies to those for whom no oral exam has been developed in his/her particular language by the Consortium for Language Access in the Courts (CLAC)) must: 1) Complete the orientation workshop for Interpreters in Nevada courts offered by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC), 2) Pass the Nevada written exam given by the AOC (minimum score of 80%), 3) Undergo the oral proficiency interview (OPI) by ALTA Language Services (score of at least 12) or Language Testing International (rating of "Superior" proficiency), 4) Completed the Nevada court observation requirement of 40 hours, 5) Submit the Certification Request application which includes a criminal history check, 6) Swear to the required oath and the Code…
32-20501.agency: Supreme Court of Nevada · Administrative Office of the Courts

32-15701.title: Psychologist
32-15701.description: Psychologists working in private practices, as well as those working for the Nevada State Department of Human Resources, must be licensed through the Board of Psychological Examiners. (Psychologists who intend to work in public schools must meet the requirements necessary to obtain an endorsement through the Department of Education. Requirements for school psychologists are listed separately.) Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 and of good moral character. 2) Have a doctoral degree from an accredited institution in an APA-accredited program or a regionally accredited program shown to be equivalent. 3) Have completed pre and post doctoral supervised experience under a licensed psychologist (1,750 hours in each). 4) Pass a national written examination. 5) Pass a State Board examination. 6) Submit fingerprints for a background check. Note on Psychological Interns and Assistants: individuals must register with the Board as a psychological intern if they wish to obtain predoctoral internship supervised experience and as a psychological assistant if they wish to obtain the postdoctoral supervised experience required for licensure. Visit the Board's website for registration requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application--$100; state examination--$270; license certificate--$25; biennial license renewal--$500; late license renewal penalty--$100; psychological assist…

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

32-11314.title: Steel Reinforcing & Erection Contractor (C14)
32-11314.description: Applicants must: 1) Have four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification in which he/she is applying. The experience must have been obtained within the preceding 10 years. Training received at an accredited college or university may be used to satisfy a portion of the required experience. 2) Prove financial responsibility (the board determines the amount of the bond that will be required.) 3) Possess good character and provide 4 reference certificates from individuals with firsthand knowledge of the applicant's experience. 4) Pass the Contractors Management Survey (CMS) exam. 5) Pass the applicable trade exam, if required for the specific license. Exams are given daily in Las Vegas, on various days in Reno, and on a limited basis in Elko. Visit the website for more detailed information on the requirements and application process. Sub classifications in this license category include: reinforcing steel; structural steel; ornamental metal; curtain walls; metal doors and windows; store fronts; prefabricated steel structures; awnings and louvres; rigging and cranes. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial application--$300; initial license and biennial renewal--$600; Residential Recovery Fund Assessment (for residential contractors only) based upon monetary license limit--$200 - $1,000; CMS and Trade exam…

32-17901.title: Elementary School Teacher
32-17901.description: An elementary license authorizes the holder to teach kindergarten* through eighth grade (K-8). Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university and must have completed an approved program for elementary school teaching which included fifty semester hours of credit in specified subjects. Visit the Department website for further information on requirements and course work. *There is also a special license available for teaching birth through second grade. Visit the Department website for specific information. Reciprocity: A license to teach in Nevada under state reciprocity may be issued under certain conditions. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: initial application - $161; additional endorsement - $50.

32-13901.title: Landscape Architect
32-13901.description: Applicants must have a combination of 6 or more years of education and experience in landscape architecture that is acceptable to the Board and pass the state and national exams. For example: 1) Have a bachelor's or master's in landscape architecture (or a degree in a related subject acceptable to the Board) from an approved school. 2) Have completed 2 years of post graduate work experience under the direct supervision of a registered landscape architect (or a combination of education and experience acceptable to the Board). 3) Pass a State Board examination and the national Landscape Architect Registration Exam (LARE). The national examination is administered by CLARB*. Applicants for the Landscape Architect in Training (LAIT) certificate must: 1) Be 21 years old, of good moral character and a U.S. citizen (or lawfully entitled to be in the U.S.). 2a) Have a 4 year landscape architecture degree, or 2b) Have 4 years of work experience under the supervision of a licensed landscape architect. 3) Have passed Section A and B of the LARE exam. *CLARB = Council of Landscape Architect Registration Boards. Reciprocity: For those registered in good standing in another state (or province of Canada), with no disciplinary action ever taken. Visit the Board website for specific requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: registration by exam--$175 ($100 for LAIT); national exami…

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

32-11310.title: Landscape Contractor (C10)
32-11310.description: Applicants must: 1) Have four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification in which he/she is applying. The experience must have been obtained within the preceding 10 years. Training received at an accredited college or university may be used to satisfy a portion of the required experience. 2) Prove financial responsibility (the board determines the amount of the bond that will be required.) 3) Possess good character and provide 4 reference certificates from individuals with firsthand knowledge of the applicant's experience. 4) Pass the Contractors Management Survey (CMS) exam. 5) Pass the applicable trade exam, if required for the specific license. Exams are given daily in Las Vegas, on various days in Reno, and on a limited basis in Elko. Visit the website for more detailed information on the requirements and application process. There are currently no sub classifications within this license category. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial application--$300; initial license and biennial renewal--$600; Residential Recovery Fund Assessment (for residential contractors only) based upon monetary license limit--$200 - $1,000; CMS and Trade exam: exam provider sets the fee.

32-20101.title: Attorney
32-20101.description: Those who wish to practice law in Nevada must pass the State Bar examination after graduating from a law school approved by the American Bar Association. Applicants for admission to the bar must: 1) Have received a degree of bachelor of law, or an equivalent law degree, from a law school approved by the committee on legal education and admissions of the American Bar Association. 2) Have good moral character and be willing and able to abide by the high ethical standards required of attorneys and counselors at law. 3) Have not been refused admission to or disbarred from the practice of law in any U.S. state, court or governmental agency due to unfitness of character. 4) Not be subject to any mental or emotional disorder which would render the applicant unfit to practice law. 5) Not be an abuser of alcohol or prescription drugs, or a user of illegal drugs. 6) Demonstrate financial responsibility. 7) Be in full compliance with any court order, including without limitation, spousal or child support orders. 8) Pass the written bar examination given in February and July. 9) Pass the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE) with a scale score of at least 85 no earlier than three years prior to, or no later than three years after, the year in which the applicant sits for and passes the bar examination. Note: The MPRE is administered every March, August and November by…

32-21301.title: Certified Public Librarian
32-21301.description: This certification is for employees of public libraries that serve a population under 50,000 and do not have an employee with a Master's in Library Science (MLS) performing the administrator, reference and children's librarian duties; it does not apply to individuals who hold a MLS. Applicants for certification must: 1a) Have a bachelor's degree and at least 2 years of library experience, or 1b) Have an associate degree and at least 4 years of library experience, or 1c) Have a high school diploma or GED and at least 7 years of library experience. 2) Have taken 21 semester credit hours in subjects specified by State Library and Archives. 3) Submit two fingerprint cards. 4) Provide a professional letter of recommendation. The completed application must be notarized and official transcripts are required (no photocopies).
32-21301.agency: Nevada State Library and Archives · Development Services

32-17906.title: Librarian - School
32-17906.description: To receive an endorsement as a school Library Media Specialist, a person must have a valid elementary, middle school or junior high, secondary or special teaching license (excluding a business and industry or special qualifications), and must: 1) Have completed a program for school Library Media Specialists which has been approved by the Department or a regional accrediting association, or 2) Hold a master's degree in library science with specialization in school librarianship from a school accredited by the American Library Association; or 3) Have completed 21 semester hours of course work specified by the Department. Fees are subject to change. The initial application fee is $161; additional endorsement - $50.

32-17102.title: Escrow Agents
32-17102.description: Escrow agencies and agents must be licensed in Nevada. Escrow agents must be associated with an agency to hold a license. Visit the Division website for information on the requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: escrow agent application --$100; annual renewals --$125; exam - $60/hour; escrow agency application --$500; escrow agency license or annual renewal --$200.
32-17102.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Mortgage Lending Division

32-17101.title: Mortgage Brokers, Bankers and Agents
32-17101.description: Employees of mortgage brokers who conduct mortgage activities must be licensed as Mortgage Agents. Applicants for mortgage agent licensure must meet the following requirements: 1) Have not been convicted of, or entered a plea of, no contest to a felony within the preceding 7 years, or at any time if the felony involved fraud, dishonesty or a breach of trust or money laundering. 2) Have never had a license or registration as a Mortgage Agent, Mortgage Banker, Mortgage Broker or residential mortgage loan originator revoked in this State or any other jurisdiction or had a financial services license revoked within the immediately preceding 10 years. 3) Have not made a false statement of material fact on the application. 4) Have not violated any provision of NRS chapter 645B or 645E, a regulation adopted pursuant to those provisions, or an order of the Commissioner. 5) Have demonstrated financial responsibility, character and general fitness so as to command the confidence of the community and warrant a determination that s/he will operate honestly, fairly and efficiently for the purposes of Chapter 645B or Chapter 645E of NRS. 6) Undergo a background check. 7) Have successfully completed pre-licensing and testing requirements. Mortgage brokers and bankers must also be licensed in Nevada. Visit the Division website for more information on the requirements for licensure. Fees may be…
32-17101.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Mortgage Lending Division

32-17306.title: Title Agents and Escrow Officers
32-17306.description: Title agents and escrow officers must be licensed in Nevada. Applicants must: 1) Be a Nevada resident (or reside within 50 miles of the state) and at least 18 years of age. 2) Complete pre-licensing education requirements at a state-approved school. 3) Provide proof of having at least one year of recent experience relating to title insurance that is acceptable to the Division. 4) Pass the state insurance examinations (in the lines of authority applied for) administered by Pearson VUE. 5) Provide fingerprint cards for a criminal history report. Visit the Division website for more information on the licensing requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: examination--$90; initial licensing--$195; business/agency affiliation--$60; fingerprinting --$37.50 (payable to Department of Public Safety) or $55.25 (electronic by Pearson VUE).
32-17306.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Insurance Division - Licensing Section

32-14302.title: Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
32-14302.description: Applicants for licensure by examination must: 1) Have graduated from an approved school of nursing with a nursing certificate (LPN). 2) Have passed the National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX). 3) Submit fingerprint cards (fingerprint reports must be cleared by the Board to obtain licensure). Applicants for licensure by endorsement must: 1) Have graduated from an approved school of nursing with a nursing certificate (LPN). 2) Have passed the NCLEX or State Board Test Pool Examination (SBTPE). 3) Have been licensed or registered as a LPN under the laws of another jurisdiction. 4) Submit fingerprint cards (fingerprint reports must be cleared by the Board to obtain licensure). Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application by examination--$90; application by endorsement--$95; fingerprinting - $50 (may vary); biennial renewal - $100.
32-14302.agency: Nevada State Board of Nursing · Licensure, Certification and Education

32-11703.title: Manicurist/Nail Technologist
32-11703.description: Applicants must have completed 600 hours in a program approved by the State Board; completed school through at least the 10th grade or the equivalent; be at least 18 years old; and pass the written and practical exams. If you are transferring from another state, you must have a current license in good standing, and you must prove that you have passed the national exam or you must take the written exam in Nevada. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application--$15; examination, written and practical--$110; examination, national written --$110; 2-year license--$70; 4-year license renewal--$140.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

32-16702.title: Boxing Promoter
32-16702.description: Boxing promoters must be licensed by the Athletic Commission. Visit the Commission website for further information about requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: promoters--$500; fingerprint cards - $38.25 each (NHP).
32-16702.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Athletic Commission

32-12901.title: Marriage and Family Therapist
32-12901.description: Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 years old, a U.S. citizen (or legally entitled to work in the United States), and be of good moral character. 2) Have an undergraduate degree from an accredited college or university approved by the Board. 3) Have completed residency training in psychiatry, or have a graduate degree in marriage and family therapy, psychology, or social work from an accredited institution approved by the State Board, or an equivalent combination of education and training approved by the Board. (Contact the Board for information on the required graduate coursework.) 4) Have at least 2 years of postgraduate experience in marriage and family therapy (and at least 3,000 hours of supervised experience, 1,500 of which must consist of direct client contact). 5) Pass an examination. 6) Provide three references (must be submitted directly from the references to the board.) Licensed Intern To obtain the required supervised experience indicated above, applicants must first obtain licensure as a marriage and family therapist intern. In general, applicants must meet the requirements listed above in items 1 - 3 and have a supervision agreement with an approved supervisor. Contact the Board for more information on the intern requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application--$75; examination--$220; license processing--$50; annual license--$150.
32-12901.agency: Board of Examiners for Marriage & Family Therapists, and Clinical Professional Counselors

32-21101.title: Massage Therapist
32-21101.description: Applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old. 2) Have at least 500 hours of schooling (transcripts must be submitted directly to the Board). 3) Have passed the Federation of State Massage Therapy Boards' written exam (Massage and Bodywork Licensing Exam (MBLEx)). 4) Provide a passport sized photo and a photocopy of a current state issued I.D., or alien resident card if applicable. 5) Submit to fingerprinting for a background check. Note: Visit the Federation of State Massage Therapy Board's website for more information on the MBLEx. Reciprocity: In addition to items 1-5 listed above, applicants must submit a copy of their current massage therapist/business license and have their current licensing authority submit verification of their status being in good standing with no disciplinary actions pending. This verification must be sent directly from the out-of-state board to the Nevada Board via the form provided or a letter. Fees: Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application - $100; license - $150; background check - $125; temporary license application - $100; temporary license (90 days) - $50.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-11102.title: Chiropractor's Assistant
32-11102.description: Applicants for certification must: 1) Have 12 months or 480 hours of classroom training or have 6 months of on-the-job training. 2) Be proficient in x-ray and physiotherapy techniques. 3) Pass a State Board examination. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: fingerprint processing - $38.25; application for certification--$100; examination--$60; biennial certificate renewal--$120.

32-21702.title: Flame Effects Operators and Assistants
32-21702.description: Flame effects operators and assistants must have a certificate of registration. Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 years old and be able to give written and oral orders in English. 2) Have not been convicted of a felony or have an addiction to drugs or alcohol. 3) Have a working knowledge of federal, state and local laws pertaining to the safe storage, handling and use of explosive materials. 4) Pass any exam deemed necessary by the State Fire Marshal. Visit the Fire Marshal's Office website for more information. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: operator certificate --$55; assistant certificate -- $27.50.

32-13703.title: Homeopathic Assistant
32-13703.description: Applicants must: 1) Have completed an educational program of at least 200 hours of training in homeopathy; 100 of which must be in Nevada under the supervision of a homeopathic physician (or a program deemed equivalent by the Board). Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: assistant license--$150; fingerprint cards-$50.

32-15302.title: Podiatry Hygienist
32-15302.description: Podiatry hygienists must be licensed by the State Board. Applicants must take the exam issued by the Board or work under the supervision of a Podiatrist for six months. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: license --$100; annual renewal -$100; fingerprints --$38.25 (may vary).

32-14103.title: Respiratory Therapist
32-14103.description: The following general requirements apply; contact the Board for more information. Applicants must: 1) Be of good moral character. 2) Be able to adequately speak and write in English. 3) Have a high school diploma or general equivalency diploma (GED) and an Associate (AA) degree. 4) Complete an educational program for respiratory care approved by the National Board for Respiratory Care. 5) Pass the examination as an entry-level or advanced practitioner of respiratory care administered by the National Board for Respiratory Care. 6) Be certified by the National Board for Respiratory Care. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application (non refundable) --$100; active license registration (biennial) --$200; background check - $75.

32-17909.title: Middle School and Junior High Teacher
32-17909.description: A middle school or junior high school license authorizes the holder to teach grades 7-9*. Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, and must have: 1) Completed an approved program for middle school or junior high teaching, or 2) Completed 24 semester credits in professional education approved by the Department, and 3) Completed 24 semester credits in a major field of endorsement or area of concentration. * Note: The middle school/junior high license does not qualify one to teach 9th grade in a high school setting. Visit the Department website for further information on requirements and course work. Reciprocity: A license to teach in Nevada under state reciprocity may be issued under certain conditions. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: initial application - $161; additional endorsement - $50.

32-18701.title: Laboratory Director
32-18701.description: There are three laboratory categories for director licensure: Licensed, Registered and Pulmonary Laboratory Director. To apply for licensure as a Director of a LICENSED laboratory, an applicant must: 1) Be a physician licensed by the Nevada State Board of Medical Examiners to practice medicine in the state and meet additional related certification, training or experience requirements set by the Division, OR 2) Hold a doctoral degree from an accredited institution with a major in a chemical, physical, or biological science, and be certified by one or more of the following American Boards of: Medical Microbiology, Clinical Chemistry, Bioanalysis, Medical Laboratory Immunology, Forensic Toxicology, or Medical Genetics (or have qualifications equivalent to certification.) An applicant for licensure as a director of a licensed laboratory for pulmonary conditions must be a physician licensed to practice in Nevada and must be certified by the American Board of Internal Medicine in the subspecialty of pulmonary disease. To apply for licensure as a Director of a REGISTERED laboratory, an applicant must: 1) Be a physician licensed by the Nevada State Board of Medical Examiners to practice medicine in the state and: a) Have at least 1 year of experience directing or supervising non-waived laboratory testing in an approved laboratory; or b) Have at least 20 credit hours of continuing medi…
32-18701.agency: Nevada Division of Public & Behavioral Health · Bureau of Health Care Quality & Compliance

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

32-14304.title: Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA)
32-14304.description: Applicants for CRNA certification by examination must: 1) Meet all requirements for Registered Nurse licensure (have an active RN license). 2) Have a master's degree in nursing or anesthetic care from an approved school. Applicants for CRNA certification by endorsement must: 1) Meet all requirements for Registered Nurse licensure (have an active RN license). 2) Have an official transcript sent directly to the Board by the educational institution that granted their master's degree in nursing or anesthetic care (if the nurse anesthetist program was completed on or after June 1, 2005)*. *Note: For those who graduated from an nurse anesthetist program between June 1, 1988 and May 31, 2005, the official transcript must be sent directly to the State Board from the educational institution that granted their bachelor's degree in nursing. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application/initial certificate--$200; biennial certificate renewal--$200.
32-14304.agency: Nevada State Board of Nursing · Licensure, Certification and Education

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-14501.title: Occupational Therapist
32-14501.description: Applicants must: 1) Have graduated with a bachelors or masters degree in Occupational Therapy (official transcripts required). 2) Passed the national exam given by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). 3) Provide verification of certification from NBCOT (must be sent directly to the Board by NBCOT). If licensed in another state, verification must be sent directly to the Board from the licensing agency in that state. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application--$150; license--$250; license renewal--$175.

32-12301.title: Optician
32-12301.description: Applicants must pass the Nevada state optical exam. To qualify for the exam, applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old, and of good moral character, and have graduated from an accredited high school or its equivalent. 2) Hold current American Board of Opticianry (ABO) & National Contact Lens Exam (NCLE) certifications. 3a) Have completed an approved opthalmic education course and have 3 years of opthalmic dispensing experience as a licensed NV apprentice dispensing optician under the supervision of a licensed optician, ophthalmologist or optometrist; or 3b) Have graduated from an approved school with an associate of applied science degree in ophthalmic technology and had 1 year of ophthalmic dispensing experience as a licensed NV apprentice under the supervision of a licensed dispensing optician, ophthalmologist or optometrist. 4) Have completed at least 100 hours of training and experience in fitting and filling contact lens prescriptions (under direct supervision as listed above). 5) Have 3 letters of reference, including one from a dispensing optician or a person who has worked in the optical industry with the applicant; letters must be mailed directly to the Board by the authors. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: apprentice application--$100; optician application/examination--$350; optician examination retake--$250; annual optician license renewal --$300; annual app…

32-14701.title: Optometrist
32-14701.description: Applicants must: 1) Have graduated from an approved school of optometry. 2) Pass the national board examination. 3) Pass a state examination (75% minimum score) on the laws and regulations governing the practice of optometry in Nevada. If an optometrist is certified to administer and prescribe therapeutic pharmaceutical agents (TPA), she/he is required to obtain 30 hours of continuing education for annual renewal, 15 hours of which must be therapeutic-related. If an optometrist is NOT certified in therapeutics (designated as diagnostic pharmaceutical agents (DPA)), eighteen hours of continuing education are required for annual renewal. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: examination--$250; initial license--$25; annual license renewal--$350.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

32-14502.title: Occupational Therapy Assistant
32-14502.description: Applicants must: 1) Have graduated with an Associate degree (official transcripts required). 2) Passed the national exam given by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). 3) Provide verification of certification from NBCOT (must be sent directly to the Board by NBCOT). 4) Provide verification of supervision by an Occupational Therapist licensed in Nevada. If licensed in another state, verification must be sent directly to the Board from the licensing agency in that state. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: application--$150; license--$175; license renewal--$125.

32-11304.title: Painting and Decorating Contractor (C4)
32-11304.description: Applicants must: 1) Have four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification in which he/she is applying. The experience must have been obtained within the preceding 10 years. Training received at an accredited college or university may be used to satisfy a portion of the required experience. 2) Prove financial responsibility (the board determines the amount of the bond that will be required.) 3) Possess good character and provide 4 reference certificates from individuals with firsthand knowledge of the applicant's experience. 4) Pass the Contractors Management Survey (CMS) exam. 5) Pass the applicable trade exam, if required for the specific license. Exams are given daily in Las Vegas, on various days in Reno, and on a limited basis in Elko. Visit the website for more detailed information on the requirements and application process. Sub classifications in this license category include: painting; wall covering; taping and finishing; sandblasting; drywall; sheet metal studs; acoustical tile; urethane coatings. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial application--$300; initial license and biennial renewal--$600; Residential Recovery Fund Assessment (for residential contractors only) based upon monetary license limit--$200 - $1,000; CMS and Trade exam: exam provider sets the fee.

32-16502.title: Pest Control Applicator - Operator or Agent
32-16502.description: Individuals applying for pest control applicator licensure in the operator/agent category must pass the appropriate examinations, but do not need to have previous pest control experience. Contact the Department of Agriculture for information on training sessions, the exam or appointments. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: examination--$25/exam; initial pest control licensing--$50; annual pest control license renewal--$50.
32-16502.agency: Deptartment of Agriculture · Plant Industry Division · Pest Control Licensing Section

32-16501.title: Pest Control Applicator - Principal
32-16501.description: Major fields of pest control are aerial, agricultural-ground, and urban-structural. Specific categories of pest control are included with each major field of pest control. Individuals applying for licensure as company principals must: 1a) Have 2 years of documented pesticide application or pest control experience in the category(ies) applied for; or 1b) Have a combination of 6 months of documented pesticide application or pest control experience in the category(ies) applied for and 16 college credit hours in biological science (at least 8 hours must be directly related to the field of pest control applied for.) 2) Pass the appropriate examinations. Note: Primary principals must also submit fingerprints for a background check. Contact the Department of Agriculture for information on training sessions, the exam or appointments. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: examination--$25/exam; initial pest control licensing--$50; annual pest control license renewal--$50.
32-16501.agency: Deptartment of Agriculture · Plant Industry Division · Pest Control Licensing Section

32-14901.title: Pharmacist
32-14901.description: Applicants must: 1) Have a degree in pharmacy from a school accredited by the Am. Council on Pharmaceutical Education and approved by the board. 2) Have 1,740 internship hours under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist (to fulfill this requirement you must register as an intern pharmacist and meet the state board requirements). 3) Pass a state board and a national examination (NAPLEX and MPJE)*. Reciprocity: Applicants may reciprocate from another state but must take the State Board examination. (Those reciprocating from California must have taken the NAPLEX exam.) Graduates from foreign schools must pass the FPGEC, TOFEL and TSE exams before taking the national and state exams. *Notes: NAPLEX = No. American Pharmacist Licensure Exam; MPJE = Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Exam. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application (includes registration) --$330; examination--$680 (paid to NABP); reciprocity--$330; license renewal--$180; intern application-- $40.

32-14902.title: Pharmaceutical Technician
32-14902.description: Pharmaceutical technicians and pharmaceutical technicians-in-training must register with the State Board. They may practice in all pharmacy settings under the direction of a pharmacist registered with the Nevada Board of Pharmacy. Pharmacy Technician applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old. 2) Have a high school degree or the equivalent. 3) Have not been convicted of a misdemeanor or felony that involves moral turpitude, dishonesty or the unlawful possession, sale or use of drugs. 4) Have no history of drug abuse. In addition applicants must meet one of the following requirements: 1) Be licensed or registered as a pharmaceutical technician in another state that licenses pharmaceutical technicians or, 2) Have completed at least 1,500 hours in Nevada as a registered pharmaceutical technician-in-training or, 3) Have graduated from a school accredited by the Am. Society of Healthsystem Pharmacists (ASHP) and have completed 350 hours in Nevada as a registered pharmaceutical technician-in-training or, 4) Graduated from a school in another state that is not accredited by the ASHP and have passed the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board's (PTCB) national exam or, 5) Have passed the PTCB exam and completed 500 hours in Nevada as a registered technician-in-training. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: registration--$40; renewal--$40.

32-15101.title: Physical Therapist
32-15101.description: Applicants must: 1) Have completed a curriculum of physical therapy approved by the Board (official transcripts required). 2) Pass the national examination. 3) Submit fingerprints, photo, original transcripts and references with application. Notes: Application signature must be notarized. A minimum of 1.5 continuing education units are required for physical therapist license renewal. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application and initial license--$300; national examination--$370; testing center fee--$85; examination processing fee--$25; fingerprinting--$37.50; annual license renewal--$150.

00-80.title: Marine Physician Assistant
00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A physician assistant must also have training as a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-80.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-10502.title: Osteopathic Physician's Assistant
32-10502.description: Applicants must: 1) Be of good moral character. 2) Be able to adequately speak and write in English. 3) Have graduated from a physician assistant program that is accredited by: a) the Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant, OR b) if graduation occurred before January 1, 2001, the Committee on Allied Health Education and Accreditation, or the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs. 4) Have been certified by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants. 5) Provide fingerprints for a background check. 6) Provide verification of their credentials through the Federation Credentials Verification Service (FCVS). Note: Applicants who have not practiced for a year or more prior to applying for licensure may be required to supply evidence of clinical competence to the Board. For information on the requirements, contact the Board. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: license--$400; renewal--$250; fingerprints--$70.

32-14102.title: Physicians' Assistant
32-14102.description: The following general requirements apply; contact the Board for more information. Applicants must: 1) Be of good moral character. 2) Be able to adequately speak and write in English. 3) Have graduated from a physician assistant program approved by the American Medical Association (AMA) Committee on Allied Health Education and Accreditation. 4) Be certified by the National Commission on Certification for Physician Assistants. 5) Pass a written exam concerning the statutes and regulations relating to the practice as a physician assistant in Nevada. Applicants may be required to appear before the State Board. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application--$300; biennial registration--$400; background check - $75.

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.
00-31.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-11323.title: Drilling Wells & Installing Pumps Contractor (C23)
32-11323.description: Applicants must: 1) Have four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification in which he/she is applying. The experience must have been obtained within the preceding 10 years. Training received at an accredited college or university may be used to satisfy a portion of the required experience. 2) Prove financial responsibility (the board determines the amount of the bond that will be required.) 3) Possess good character and provide 4 reference certificates from individuals with firsthand knowledge of the applicant's experience. 4) Pass the Contractors Management Survey (CMS) exam. 5) Pass the applicable trade exam, if required for the specific license. Exams are given daily in Las Vegas, on various days in Reno, and on a limited basis in Elko. Visit the website for more detailed information on the requirements and application process. There are currently no sub classifications in this license category. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial application--$300; initial license and biennial renewal--$600; Residential Recovery Fund Assessment (for residential contractors only) based upon monetary license limit--$200 - $1,00; CMS and Trade exam: exam provider sets the fee.

32-15301.title: Podiatrist
32-15301.description: Applicants must: 1) Have completed the necessary undergraduate program and graduated from an accredited doctor of podiatric medicine (DPM) program. 2) Have completed an *APMA accredited, one-year residency. 3) Pass the National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners examination. 4) Pass the American Podiatric Medical examination Part III administered by the National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (contact the board for more information on the required examinations). 5) Submit fingerprints for a background check. 6) Submit letters of verification from the hospitals and surgical centers where you had privileges in the last year. *American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA). If an applicant is currently licensed in another state, a certificate from that state's licensing board is required. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application --$600 ($100 of this fee is not refundable); annual license renewal--$400; fingerprints --$38.25 (may vary).

32-19704.title: Private Investigator
32-19704.description: Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 years old and of good moral character. 2) Undergo a background check through FBI and DPS. 3) Have no criminal or felony convictions involving moral turpitude or illegal use or possession of a dangerous weapon. 4) Have 5 years (10,000 hours) of investigative experience certified by their employer, or a combination of education and experience acceptable to the board. 5) Pass a State Board examination with a score of 75% or better. 6) Obtain at least $200,000 worth of liability insurance. A licensee must be certified by a board-certified firearm instructor if he/she must carry a firearm while on duty. A certification card is issued upon completion of the firearms course. In addition to the fees listed below, a background investigation deposit fee is also required and is applied to the cost of conducting an investigation. The fee is $750 for the first license category and $250 for each additional license category. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application processing --$20; examination--$100 (nonrefundable); abeyance fee--$100 per license per year; initial license--license fee is prorated; annual license renewal--$500 per license; firearms initial certification--$100; annual firearms certification renewal--$50; fingerprints--$38.25.

00-05.title: Customs Broker
00-05.description: Customs brokers must pass an exam to obtain a license. Further information can be found at the US Customs Service web site: http://www.customs.gov/xp/cgov/import/broker_management/.

00-59.title: Purser
00-59.description: The Purser, one of a ship's staff officers, is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A Junior Assistant Purser requires no experience. A Senior Assistant Purser requires 180 days, a Purser requires 360 days, and a Chief Purser requires 720 days of service aboard vessels while performing duties related to the purser's office. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-59.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-17506.title: Licensed Energy Auditor
32-17506.description: Applicants must: 1) Have a high school diploma or the equivalent and be at least 18 years old. 2) Provide proof of certification or accreditation from an organization approved by the Division. 3) Provide proof of completing and passing at least 40 hours of related building science training and practice from a training provider approved by the Division. 4) Submit proof of insurance coverage specified by the Division. 5) Submit 2 fingerprint cards (or electronic verification issued from an approved vendor). Fee: Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application--$350; fingerprint card processing--$38.25 (payable to Dept. of Public Safety); renewal--$250.
32-17506.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Real Estate Division

32-17905.title: Psychologist - School
32-17905.description: Psychologists employed in schools must obtain an endorsement from the Department of Education. (Private practice psychologists must be licensed through the Board of Psychological Examiners. Requirements for private practice psychologists are listed separately.) To qualify for an endorsement to serve as a school psychologist, a person must: 1) Hold a graduate degree from an accredited college or university with a concentration in school psychology and; 2) Have successfully completed the course work and earned the graduate credits required by the Department and; 3) Have completed an internship in school psychology as outlined in the Department's practicum requirements. Or, a person must: 4) Hold a certificate as a nationally certified school psychologist issued by the National School Psychology Certification System of the National Association of School Psychologists, or 5) Have completed a program approved by the Department which prepares a person to be a school psychologist. Fees are subject to change. The initial application fee is $161.

32-15102.title: Physical Therapist Assistant
32-15102.description: Applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old. 2) Completed a curriculum for physical therapist assistant approved by the State Board. 3) Pass a national examination. 4) Submit fingerprints, photo, original transcripts (including high school) and references with application. Notes: Application signature must be notarized. The physical therapist assistant curriculum must be at least a 2-year program requiring a minimum of 60 semester hours at an accredited school. A minimum of 1.5 continuing education units are required for physical therapist assistant license renewal. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application and initial license--$200; national examination--$370; testing center fee--$70; examination processing fee--$25; fingerprinting--$37.50; annual license renewal--$100.

32-18801.title: Mammography Technologist
32-18801.description: Applicants for certification must: 1) Have valid general radiographer credentials from the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) or another organization approved by the Division. 2) Provide proof of advanced training in mammography (at least 40 hours) accredited by a recognized credentialing institution such as ASRT or ARRT. Contact the Division for further information on approved training. Additional Notes: If you have been mammography qualified for over 3 years, you must provide proof of at least 15 CEU's in mammography obtained within the prior 3 years. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application --$88.
32-18801.agency: Radiation Control Program · Nevada Division of Public & Behavioral Health · Bureau of Healthcare Quality & Compliance

32-17502.title: Real Estate Salesperson
32-17502.description: Applicants must have 90 hours or 6 semester credits of classroom instruction in real estate principles, practices and law from a Nevada Real Estate Commission accredited provider. The course must include a minimum of 18 hours of Nevada law, consisting of NRS 645, 119, 119A, 119B and their respective administrative codes. Certified transcripts must be submitted with the license application. Applicants must show proof of passing the national and Nevada state exams within one year of the application date. Continuing education hours are required for renewal of active status licenses. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: examination (standard)--$100; initial license--$85; license renewal--$140 (2-year). In addition to the initial license and license renewal fees there is a mandatory education, research, and recovery fund fee of $40 (initial) and $80 (renewal).
32-17502.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Real Estate Division

32-17501.title: Real Estate Broker
32-17501.description: Categories of licensure are "broker" and "broker/salesperson". Applicants for Real Estate Broker/Salesperson must have 64 college semester units combining real estate, business, economics, and other college-level courses and pass state and national examinations. Required education courses include 9 units of real estate principles, practices, law, and appraisal; 15 units of courses in business, economics, or other real estate topics (such as finance); 3 units of broker management training and 37 units of college courses other than those listed above. Active full time experience may be applied toward completion of the total educational requirement, with the exception of 18 hours of Nevada law and the 3 units of broker management training. (Two years of experience equals 16 semester units.) Categories of Real Estate Broker license for those who wish to be licensed as a "broker of record" (a real estate broker who operates his/her own business) are "corporate," "partner," "individual," or "associate." In addition to the requirements specified for Real Estate Broker/Salesperson, applicants must submit a personal financial statement; must have been actively engaged as a full time licensed real estate broker/salesperson for at least 2 of the 4 years immediately prior to the issuance of the broker's license; pass state and national examinations. Continuing education hours are required…
32-17501.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Real Estate Division

32-18705.title: Music Therapist
32-18705.description: Music Therapists must be licensed in Nevada. Applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old. 2) Have completed an academic program approved by the American Music Therapy Association with a bachelor's or higher degree in music therapy. 3) Provide proof of current board certification from the Certification Board for Music Therapists (if applicable). 4) Provide 2 sets of fingerprints for a criminal history check. (Note: NRS 640D.170- Grounds for license denial, suspension or revocation.) Note: 100 units of continuing education are required for renewal (every 3 years.) Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: license --$200 (valid 3 years); fingerprints--$37.50
32-18705.agency: Nevada Division of Public & Behavioral Health · Bureau of Health Care Quality & Compliance

32-19201.title: Motor Vehicle Salesperson
32-19201.description: Vehicle salespersons and managers must be licensed. Applicants must submit the application packet, a waiver form for a criminal history check, two sets of fingerprints (on cards supplied by the Department) and the certificate of employment form completed by a licensed Nevada vehicle dealer. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: license --$75; annual renewal --$40; transfer fee --$20.
32-19201.agency: Department of Motor Vehicles · Occupational & Business Licensing

00-61.title: Professional Nurse
00-61.description: A ship's Professional Nurse is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A professional nurse must also hold a valid license as a registered nurse issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-61.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-14301.title: Registered Nurse (RN)
32-14301.description: Applicants for licensure by examination must: 1) Have graduated from an approved school of nursing with a diploma or nursing degree. 2) Have passed the National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX). 3) Submit fingerprint cards (fingerprint reports must be cleared by the Board to obtain licensure). Applicants for licensure by endorsement must: 1) Have graduated from an approved school of nursing with a diploma or nursing degree. 2) Have passed the NCLEX or State Board Test Pool Examination (SBTPE). 3) Have been licensed or registered as a RN under the laws of another jurisdiction. 4) Submit fingerprint cards (fingerprint reports must be cleared by the Board to obtain licensure). Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application by examination--$100; application by endorsement--$105; fingerprinting - $50 (may vary); biennial renewal - $100.
32-14301.agency: Nevada State Board of Nursing · Licensure, Certification and Education

00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html
00-03.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-30.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-04.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-32.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-17908.title: Exceptional Pupils Endorsements
32-17908.description: The Nevada Department of Education issues the following types of endorsements for licensed* teachers to teach exceptional pupils at various grade levels: Adapted Physical Education, Autism, Early Childhood Developmentally Delayed, (Limited) Generalist, Gifted and Talented, Hearing Impairments, Intellectual Disabilities, Speech and Language Impairments, Visual Impairments, and Orientation and Mobility. *See the licensure requirements for elementary and secondary teachers. Visit the Department website for information on specific endorsement requirements. Fees are subject to change. The initial application fee is $161. An additional endorsement is $50.

32-17907.title: School or Program Administrator
32-17907.description: The Nevada Department of Education issues the following types of administrative endorsements: 1) Professional administrator of a school. 2) Professional administrator of a program. 3) Supervisor of curriculum and instruction. A person holding an endorsement as an administrator of a school may be employed by a school district as a superintendent, principal, assistant superintendent, vice principal, administrative assistant, supervisor, or coordinator of various programs. An endorsement as an administrator of a program is necessary to supervise or coordinate a program of: nursing, psychology (as it is applied in a school), speech therapy, physical therapy or occupational therapy. Visit the Department website for specific licensure and coursework requirements. Fees are subject to change. The initial application fee is $161. An additional endorsement is $50.

32-17904.title: Counselor - School
32-17904.description: School counselors must have an elementary or secondary counseling endorsement. To qualify for an endorsement to serve as an elementary or secondary school counselor, a person must: 1) Hold a master's or more advanced degree in school counseling, or 2) Hold a specialty credential as a National Certified Counselor issued by the National Board for Certified Counselors, or 3) Hold a master's or a more advanced degree with a major in counseling and meet the additional counseling experience and graduate coursework requirements specified by the Department, or 4) Hold a master's or a more advanced degree, and have at least 2 years of teaching or school counseling experience, and meet the additional counseling experience and graduate coursework requirements specified by the Department. Visit the Department website for more information on the additional counseling experience and coursework referred to in items 3 and 4. Fees are subject to change. The initial application fee is $161.
