00-BrokDeal.title: Series 28 - Introducing Broker/Dealer Financial and Operations Principal
00-BrokDeal.description: Covered supervisory activities include the following. ?Back office operations ?Preparation and maintenance of a member firm’s books and records ?Compliance with financial responsibility rules that apply to fully disclosed broker-dealers that do not hold customer funds and securities, and do not carry customer accounts

00-RegOpt.title: Series 4 - Registered Options Principal Examination (OP)
00-RegOpt.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over trading, market making, underwriting and advertising of: ?Equity options ?Foreign currency options ?Interest rate options ?Index options ?Options on government and mortgage-backed securities

00-MunFund.title: Series 51 - Municipal Fund Securities Limited Principal
00-MunFund.description: Municipal fund securities (e.g., 529 College Savings Plans, Local Government Investment Pools (LGIPs))

00-MunSec.title: Series 53 - Municipal Securities Principal
00-MunSec.description: Municipal securities, including municipal fund securities (e.g., 529 College Savings Plans, Local Government Investment Pools (LGIPs))

00-GenSec.title: Series 9/10 - General Securities Sales Supervisor
00-GenSec.description: The Series 9/10 Exam is designed to assess the competency of General Securities Sales Supervisors in the following fields: ?Sale of Corporate Securities ?Rights ?Warrants ?Closed-End Funds ?Money Market Funds ?REITs ?Asset-Backed Securities ?Mortgage Backed-Securities (Corporate) ?Equity Options ?Options on (corporate) Backed-Securities ?Mutual Funds ?Variable Annuities and Variable Life Insurance ?Government Securities ?Repos and Certificates of Accrual on Government Securities ?Municipal Securities and Municipal Fund Securities ?Direct Participation Programs

32-19901.title: Securities Broker-Dealer and Representative
32-19901.description: Broker-dealers that are members of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) must file pages one and two of the form BD with FINRA designating Nevada as the state requested for licensing. The registration fee for licensing in Nevada is $300 which will be taken out of the firm's Central Registration Depository (CRD) account. Broker-dealers that are not members of FINRA must file the following documents for licensure with the State Securities Division: 1) The Uniform Application for Broker-Dealer registration (Form BD). 2) A balance sheet (financial condition statement) prepared within 60 days prior to the date on which application for registration is filed, prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and accompanied by an auditor's report containing an unqualified opinion of an independent certified public accountant. 3) A $10,000 fidelity bond in a form acceptable to the Division or proof of membership in the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC). 4) Form U-4 plus proof of passing the Uniform Securities Agent State Law Exam (USASLE, Series 63 or 66 Examination) and proof that a designated official (i.e., owner, director, officer) of the broker-dealer has passed the appropriate principal exams. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial or renewal license --$300. Sales Representative: A Financial Industry Regulatory Authorit…

32-19706.title: Canine Security Handler and Trainer
32-19706.description: Canine Security Handlers and Trainers supply, train, or handle dogs for the protection or safety of people and property. Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 years old and of good moral character. 2) Undergo a background check through FBI and DPS. 3) Have no criminal or felony convictions involving moral turpitude or illegal use or possession of a dangerous weapon. 4) Obtain at least $200,000 worth of liability insurance. 5) Demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Board their ability to handle, supply and train watchdogs. In addition to the fees listed below, a background investigation deposit fee is also required and is applied to the cost of conducting an investigation. The fee is $750 for the first license category and $250 for each additional license category. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application processing --$20; examination--$100 (nonrefundable); abeyance fee--$100 per license per year; initial license--license fee is prorated; annual license renewal--$500 per license; fingerprints--$38.25.

32-19705.title: Private Patrolman
32-19705.description: Those who employ and provide watchmen, guards, patrolmen, uniformed traffic control officers, and bodyguards to protect persons or property against fire, theft, vandalism, or illegal entry must be licensed. Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 years old and of good moral character. 2) Undergo a background check through FBI and DPS. 3) Have no criminal or felony convictions involving moral turpitude or illegal use or possession of a dangerous weapon. 4) Have 5 years (10,000 hours) of private patrolman experience certified by their employer, or a combination of education and experience acceptable to the board. 5) Pass a State Board examination with a score of 75% or better. 6) Obtain at least $200,000 worth of liability insurance. A licensee must be certified by a board-certified firearm instructor if he/she must carry a firearm while on duty. A certification card is issued upon completion of the firearms course. Canine Security Handlers/Trainers must meet requirements 1-3 and 6 above. In addition, they must demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Board their ability to handle, supply and train watchdogs. In addition to the fees listed below, a background investigation deposit fee is also required and is applied to the cost of conducting an investigation. The fee is $750 for the first license category and $250 for each additional license category. Fees may be subject to change. Fee…

00-28.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary - OTI
00-28.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI) - Ocean Freight Forwarder requires that the designated employee for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-28.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

00-29.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary -NVOCC
00-29.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI)- Non-Vessel-Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) requires that the qualifying individual for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites: http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-29.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

00-67.title: Barge Supervisor
00-67.description: A Barge Supervisor is required to pass an exam, have 3 years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology, plus at least 168 days of related experience. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-67.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-37.title: Chief Mate - Upper Level
00-37.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Mate - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on Any Gross Tons oceangoing steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Second Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-37.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-34.title: Deck Officers
00-34.description: The navigation of a vessel and management of the deck department is the responsibility of the Deck Officers. Deck officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Master, Chief Mate, Second Mate, Third Mate, Mate and Operator), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam, Motor, Sail or Auxiliary Sail), vessel tonnage (from not more than 5 to any gross register tons), and route (e.g., Inland, Great Lakes, Near Coastal or Oceans). Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-34.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-40.title: Master - Lower Level
00-40.description: Obtaining a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Lower Level requires a specified amount of qualifying service based on details such as vessel size and area of operation (ocean, near coastal, Great Lakes, or inland). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-40.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-36.title: Master - Upper Level
00-36.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Chief Mate on ocean Any Gross Tons steam or motor vessels; or 180 days as Chief Mate plus 360 days as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-36.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-66.title: Offshore Installation Manager - OIM
00-66.description: An Offshore Installation Manager (OIM) requires passing an exam and four years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 168 days of related work experience. Specialized training in rig stability, oil well control or operation, firefighting and survival at sea are required. OIMs apply for an OIM Unrestricted License or one of four specialized licenses: OIM Surface Units on Location, OIM Surface Units Underway, OIM Bottom Bearing Units Underway, and OIM Bottom-Bearing Units on Location. Federal regulations can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SECTION=470&YEAR=1999&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-66.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-44.title: Pilot (Ship)
00-44.description: A license or endorsement as a Pilot is route-specific and requires experience navigating the body of water specified. A written exam and physical exam are also required. Further information on Pilot requirements can be found on the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2002-title46-vol1/CFR-2002-title46-vol1-part10.
00-44.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-69.title: Radar Observer
00-69.description: The Radar Observer certificate is issued by the United States Coast Guard to licensed deck officers. It requires specialized training and examination in radar navigation and is issued for 5 years. Further information can be found in the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10.305) at web site http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50176913269+4+2+0&WAISaction=retrieve and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-69.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-39.title: Third Mate - Upper Level
00-39.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Mate - Upper Level requires 1080 days service in the deck department of ocean steam or motor vessels with 6 months as Able Seaman (AB); or graduate from an approved marine academy; or completion of an approved 3 year apprentice mate training program; or 360 days as Master on ocean steam or motor vessels greater than 200 GT while licensed as a Master 1600 Gross Tons. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-39.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-68.title: Ballast Control Operator
00-68.description: A United States Coast Guard Ballast Control Operator is required to pass an exam and to have 1 year related experience, including at least 28 days as a trainee under a licensed Ballast Control Operator or a degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 28 days as a trainee. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://frwebgate2.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=051618583+1+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve, http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-68.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-46.title: Chief Engineer
00-46.description: To be licensed by the United States Coast Guard as a Chief Engineer, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer; or while holding a First Assistant Engineer license, complete 360 days of service as follows: a minimum of 180 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer plus a minimum of 360 days as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer, Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-46.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-51.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal)
00-51.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal) include 1,440 days at sea, with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer & 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-51.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-50.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-50.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans), include 1,800 days at sea, with 720 days as a Licensed Engineer & 900 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-50.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-53.title: Designated Duty Engineer
00-53.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Designated Duty Engineer include specified service time at sea, with experience as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED) on a vessel of specified horsepower. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-53.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-45.title: Engineering Officers
00-45.description: The propulsion plant of a vessel and management of the engineering department is the responsibility of the Engineering Officers. Engineering officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Chief Engineer, First Assistant Engineer, Second Assistant Engineer, Third Assistant Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Designated Duty Engineer), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam or Motor), horsepower (from 1,000 to any horsepower), and route (e.g., Near Coastal or Oceans). License limitations for deck and engineering officers, including tonnage and horsepower, are based on the type of experience of each applicant and the passing of applicable written examinations. Each license has separate general, service and examination requirements. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-45.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

32-17701.title: Taxicab Driver
32-17701.description: Except in Clark County, taxicab companies in Nevada are licensed by the state's Transportation Authority (NTA). The NTA does not license taxi drivers. In general, those employed as taxi drivers (outside of Clark County) are required to have a valid driver's license (Class C) and will be referred by their employer to a local law enforcement agency for a background check. The requirements for taxicab drivers in Clark County are listed separately.
32-17701.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Nevada Transportation Authority

32-17801.title: Taxicab Driver - Las Vegas Area
32-17801.description: In the Clark County/Las Vegas area, taxi driver permits are issued by the Taxicab Authority. To apply for a permit, applicants must be referred by their employer. Applications must be completed in the Authority office and will not be allowed out. Requirements include: 1) Referral Sheet and Authorization of Information Sheet from a taxicab company; 2) Valid Nevada Driver's License (Class C); 3) Proof of 30 days residency and addresses for the last 3 years; 4) Last place of employment; 5) Listing of all prior convictions and pending court cases on the application form; 6) Ability to read, speak and understand English (electronic test given); 7) Physical by a medical doctor (DOT physical); 8) Completion of the Drivers Awareness Program (DAP); and 9) Fingerprints for a background check. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: application - $40; renewals, replacement or change of listed employer - $10; fingerprints - $51.25.
32-17801.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Taxicab Authority

32-12501.title: Speech Pathologist
32-12501.description: Speech pathologists practicing in the state must be licensed through the Board. Those persons working in the school districts must be licensed through the Department of Education and are not required to maintain the state licensure, however, if they also work outside of the schools, both would be required. Applicants must: 1) Be of good moral character. 2) Have a master's degree or higher in Speech Pathology from an accredited college (official transcripts required) or possess equivalent training and experience as determined by the Board. 3) Hold current American Speech-Language & Hearing Association (ASHA) certification. For more information on the requirements or on special licenses (temporary, provisional and limited) visit the Board website. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial application/license--$250; annual license renewal--$100.

32-16704.title: Referee (Professional Ring Officials)
32-16704.description: Professional Ring Officials (referees, timekeepers and judges) must be licensed by the Athletic Commission. Applicants must be at least 21 years old and not have been convicted of a felony or other crime involving turpitude. The Commission determines when additional ring officials are needed and when the licensing exam will be conducted. Visit the Commission website for further information about requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: referees--$75; timekeepers and judges--$50; ringside doctor--$100.
32-16704.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Athletic Commission

32-16703.title: Timekeeper or Judge (Professional Ring Officials)
32-16703.description: Professional Ring Officials (referees, timekeepers and judges) must be licensed by the Athletic Commission. Applicants must be at least 21 years old and not have been convicted of a felony or other crime involving turpitude. The Commission determines when additional ring officials are needed and when the licensing exam will be conducted. Visit the Commission website for further information about requirements. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: referees--$75; timekeepers and judges--$50; ringside doctor--$100.
32-16703.agency: Department of Business & Industry · Athletic Commission

32-15502.title: Land Surveyor
32-15502.description: Applicants must: 1) Be at least 21 years old, of good character and good reputation. 2) Pass a 2-hour Nevada State Board land surveying examination. 3) Pass the Fundamentals of Land Surveying (LSI) exam.* 4) Pass the Principles and Practice of Land Surveying (PLS) examination.* Note: An applicant for the PLS exam must have completed a 4 year approved college program in surveying and have 4 years of experience in land surveying. *National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES) exams (8-hour and 6-hour written tests.) To be eligible for certification as a land surveyor intern applicants must: 1) Be a graduate of, or in the final year of, a land-surveying or engineering curriculum of 4 years approved by the board. 2) Have passed the Fundamentals of Land Surveying (LSI) exam. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application and exam (professional land surveyor)--$200; biennial license renewal (professional land surveyor)--$100; application for Fundamentals/Intern (LSI) exam--$30; PLS Nevada specific exam--$100.
32-15502.agency: Board of Professional Engineers & Land Surveyors

32-19903.title: Athlete's Agent
32-19903.description: Athlete's agents must hold a certificate of registration in Nevada. For information, application form and instructions visit the Division website. Fees are subject to change. Fees are: application Fee --$500; biennial renewal--$500.

00-64.title: Enrolled Agent - EA
00-64.description: Requirements to become an enrolled agent of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) are one of the following (1) pass an exam; or (2) document 5 years of relevant experience as an employee for the IRS. Continuing professional education hours every three-year cycle is required for renewal of the credential. Further information can be found at the IRS web site: http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/agents/index.html.
00-64.agency: Internal Revenue Service · Enrolled Practitioner Program Unit

32-11320.title: Tiling Contractor (C20)
32-11320.description: Applicants must: 1) Have four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification in which he/she is applying. The experience must have been obtained within the preceding 10 years. Training received at an accredited college or university may be used to satisfy a portion of the required experience. 2) Prove financial responsibility (the board determines the amount of the bond that will be required.) 3) Possess good character and provide 4 reference certificates from individuals with firsthand knowledge of the applicant's experience. 4) Pass the Contractors Management Survey (CMS) exam. 5) Pass the applicable trade exam, if required for the specific license. Exams are given daily in Las Vegas, on various days in Reno, and on a limited basis in Elko. Visit the website for more detailed information on the requirements and application process. Sub classifications in this license category include: plastic tile and wallboard; swimming pool tile and coping. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: initial application--$300; initial license and biennial renewal--$600; Residential Recovery Fund Assessment (for residential contractors only) based upon monetary license limit--$200 - $1,000; CMS and Trade exam: exam provider sets the fee.

00-79.title: Aircraft Dispatcher
00-79.description: An Aircraft Dispatcher certificate requires that the individual has work experience as an aircraft dispatcher or related occupation such as pilot. Training in aircraft dispatching and passing written and practical tests are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.51-65.70, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ

32-19101.title: Commercial Driver's License
32-19101.description: Different classes of commercial drivers' licenses are issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) depending on the number of people being transported and/or the size of the vehicle being driven. People who drive commercial vehicles weighing 26,001 or more pounds must have a Class A or Class B commercial driver's license. The type of license depends on whether the vehicle is a combination type such as a tractor-trailer (Class A) or a single type such as a dump truck or a bus (Class B). People who drive vehicles to transport hazardous materials or drive vehicles weighing 26,000 pounds or less designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver, must have a Class C commercial driver's license. Types of endorsements that may be added to the commercial driver's license include the following: double/triple trailers (T); passenger transport (P); school bus driver (S) (also requires a (P) endorsement); tank vehicle (N); hazardous materials (H); and hazardous materials and tank vehicle (X). Applicants must pass a different knowledge test for each endorsement. A skills test is also required to add a passenger transport (P) endorsement or a school bus driver (S) endorsement. To obtain a CDL, applicants must be at least 21 years old for interstate transport or for a passenger (P) or hazardous materials (H) endorsement. Applicants who are 18-20 years old may be issued a…
32-19101.agency: Department of Motor Vehicles · Commercial Driver's License Center

32-15903.title: Euthanasia Technician
32-15903.description: People who work for organizations that euthanize animals using controlled substances must be trained and licensed by the Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners. The one-day training is scheduled once or twice per year. Participants must pass a written and practical exam to receive a certificate. Those receiving a euthanasia technician certificate are also registered with the Board of Pharmacy. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: examinations/initial licensing--$200; annual license renewal--$100.

32-15902.title: Veterinary Technician
32-15902.description: Veterinary technicians working in veterinary hospitals must be licensed. Applicants must: 1a) Have graduated from an animal health technology program approved by the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA), by the state Education Department (or its equivalent in the state where the college is located) or by the Board, or 1b) Have a bachelor's in an animal science related field and meet the experience requirement listed in item 1d, or 1c) Complete an accelerated veterinary technician program approved by the board and meet the experience requirement listed in item 1d. 1d) Options 1b and 1c must provide proof of at least 4,000 hours of supervised clinical experience in a veterinary hospital that is verified by an active, practicing veterinarian. 2) Pass the Nevada Veterinary Technician Jurisprudence Examination (covering applicable state laws). 3) Pass the Veterinary Technician National Examination (VTNE) which is offered three times per year. 4) Provide a letter of recommendation from a person associated with the practice of veterinary medicine. Veterinary Technician-in-Training: Candidates must be 18 years of age, have a high school diploma or equivalent, be of good moral character, be enrolled in a school or program of training that is approved by the AVMA or the Board, and participate in training while on the job. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: Nevada jurispr…

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

32-15901.title: Veterinarian
32-15901.description: Applicants must: 1) Have completed a four-year veterinary medicine program at a school approved by the American Veterinary Medical Association with course work emphasizing the area of specialization. 2a) Pass the national board (NBE) and clinical competency (CCT) examinations; or 2b) Pass the North American Veterinary Licensing Examination (NAVLE) within 5 years of application. 3) Pass a State Board jurisprudence examination. The Board accepts candidates for the Nevada examination who are within a year of graduating. The applicant must submit a letter of good standing from the dean of the school from which he/she will graduate. Applicants who have been licensed in another state must submit a letter of good standing from the state in which he/she is currently licensed as well as a letter of good standing from each state in which he/she was previously licensed. Applicants who have completed a veterinary medicine program outside the U.S. must also present the Education Committee of Foreign Veterinary Graduates (ECFVG) certificate to the Board before being accepted to take the examination. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: application/examination/initial licensing--$200; annual license renewal (active status)--$250; annual license renewal (inactive status)--$130.

requirements.label: Exam

32-22301.title: Water Treatment or Distribution Center Operator Certificate
32-22301.description: Applicants must: 1) Be at least 18 years old. 2) Have a high school diploma or G.E.D. 3) Pass a written exam. Note: Higher grades of certification require completion of additional postsecondary instruction approved by the Bureau. The type and size of the water system will determine the type and grade level of certification needed. Contact the Bureau for specific information. Fees may be subject to change. Fees are: full certificate - $84; operator-in-training certificate- $57; certificate by reciprocity - $57.
